title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
body: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube , ai , generative-ai , llms , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai-misuse

title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
body: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary. In practice, that looks like this: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama'; SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); That returns a value like 0/0306EE20 . Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s'); SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama'; The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch up within the specified time. README 節錄：# ung220z-tool 针对 **UNG220Z（九联 / Unionman 中国移动光猫）** 的一键凭据提取工具。 > ⚠️ 仅用于**你自己的设备**，用于找回自己忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。 > 未经授权对他人设备使用属于违法行为，作者不承担任何责任。 ## 背景 这类光猫的 Web 管理页基于 `.gch` CGI 框架，登录口令由 TR-069 定期轮换，普通用户拿到的密码往往几天就失效。本工具走 Telnet 通道，直接读取设备配置库，拿到**当下有效**的全部凭据。 ## 工作流程 ``` 用户输入账号密码 ↓ 拼出 http:// /usr= &psw= &cmd=1&telnet.gch 并打开浏览器（同时脚本直连兜底） ↓ Telnet 登录 → root shell ↓ sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml 解密配置 ↓ 提取 Web 账号 / Telnet 口令 / PPPoE / WiFi 密钥 / root 口令 ↓ 打印凭据表 + 落盘日志 ``` ## 用法 ```bash python3 ung220z.py ``` 会依次询问： ``` ※ 用户名和密码通常印在光猫【背面贴纸】上（S/N 标签） 形如「用户名：user 密码：xxxxxxxx」，把光猫翻过来就能看到 ① 光猫地址 [192.168.1.1]: ② 用户名 [user]: ③ 密码（输入时不显示） 密码: ``` 也可以全部走命令行： ```bash python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码' python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码' --no-browser ``` ### 常用参数 | 参数 | 说明 | |---|---| | `-i, --ip` | 光猫地址，默认 `192.168.1.1` | | `-u, --user` | 登录用户名，默认 `user` | | `-p, --password` | 登录密码，不填则交互输入 | | `--telnet-user` | Telnet 用户名，默认 `CMCCAdmin` | | `--telnet-password` | Telnet 口令（部分机型与 Web 口令不同） | | `--no-browser` | 不调用浏览器，纯 HTTP 请求 | | `--unlock` | Web 被会话锁占住时重启 httpd 解锁 | | `--no-release` | 不尝试释放残留 Web 会话 | ## 输出示例 ``` [22:15:00] INFO 会话开始 目标=192.168.1.1 账户=user [22:15:00] HTTP 已发送给浏览器: http://192.168.1.1/usr=user&psw=***&cmd=1&telnet.gch [22:15:00] HTTP telnet.gch → TelnetSet Success!
